choices.label: Buy, and ask nothing
choices.outcomeText: The boat is empty by evening and gone by morning. It was a very good price. Somewhere upriver, a settlement is counting a loss and beginning to ask where it went.

choices.label: Send him on
choices.outcomeText: He shrugs, casts off, and takes his cargo to the next landing, where it will be somebody else's decision.

choices.label: Hold him and find out
choices.outcomeText: It costs you the trade and three days. What you learn is not about him. It is about who is moving goods through your territory without your knowledge, and how long they have been doing it.

choices.label: Ask the traders about him
choices.outcomeText: The trader with the tally-stick told this road you were good for a debt nobody could have made you pay. That buys you a straight answer: the cargo came off a landing two days north, and the men who loaded it were not the men who owned it.

choices.label: Run him off
choices.outcomeText: He breaks camp without argument and rides out at a walk, which is its own kind of statement. He does not look back and he does not hurry.

choices.label: Set a watch and wait
choices.outcomeText: For four more days he does nothing worth reporting. On the fifth the camp is cold and the ground is swept, and your watchers cannot say when he left.

choices.label: Bring him in and feed him
choices.outcomeText: He eats like a man who has been rationing, thanks your people once, and answers no questions at all. In the morning he is gone, and the blanket is folded.

choices.label: Give them iron
choices.outcomeText: You hand over more spikes and plate than you meant to. The foreman logs it in a book with a great many other entries in it.

choices.label: Put your people on the line
choices.outcomeText: Your unit stays and works. It is not soldiering and nobody pretends otherwise, and the gap closes faster than it had any right to.

choices.label: Leave them to it
choices.outcomeText: The foreman nods and goes back to work. It costs her nothing to be refused; she has been refused before.

choices.label: Tell her you'll return
choices.outcomeText: She takes you at your word, writes nothing down, and gets back on the line.

choices.label: Agree to help hold it open
choices.outcomeText: No treaty, no seal, no flag on the post. An understanding between your seat and a woman with a hammer, which on this stretch of ground is worth more than either.

choices.label: Accept their choice and go
choices.outcomeText: They have found someone else to trust with the track. The foreman says she hopes you share their ideals, and she says it without irony, which is worse.

choices.label: Take the junction
choices.outcomeText: You put your own people on the post and your own mark on the line. The crew stop working and stand there watching, and one of them is already walking east to tell somebody.

choices.label: Track the herd's back trail
choices.outcomeText: Six miles of trampled ground and nothing else. Whatever turned them did not leave a print.

choices.label: Note it and move on
choices.outcomeText: You mark it on the route log. It is the kind of entry that means nothing until something else is written under it.

choices.label: Give them water and let them go
choices.outcomeText: They are gone inside the hour. The woman's account stays with your people longer than she does, and gets repeated more accurately each time it is retold, which is how these things work.

choices.label: Press them for detail
choices.outcomeText: You get names, a direction, and a date. You do not get one thing anybody witnessed. The children are the only ones who will describe it, and what they describe does not agree.

choices.label: Turn south
choices.outcomeText: Three days out of your way. What you find is nobody's idea of an answer, but it is yours alone, and nothing that happens later will surprise you as much as it surprises everyone else.

choices.label: Keep to your route
choices.outcomeText: You make good time. The southern branch stays where it is.

choices.label: Honor the tally
choices.outcomeText: You pay a debt you did not incur, to a man you have never met, for a promise made by someone in the ground. He does not thank you effusively. He puts both halves of the stick in the fire.

choices.label: Refuse the tally
choices.outcomeText: You tell him the dead don't sign for the living. He accepts this without heat, puts the stick away, and does not leave the road.

choices.label: Pay part of it
choices.outcomeText: He takes what you offer and keeps the stick, which means the matter is not closed and both of you know it.

choices.label: Let him follow
choices.outcomeText: He keeps his distance and his mouth open. By the third settlement, the story has arrived before you do.

choices.label: Settle with him now
choices.outcomeText: You catch him up on the road and close it properly, in front of witnesses who will be repeating this for a year.

choices.label: Let him speak for you
choices.outcomeText: He stands up at a trade table and says your faction paid a debt it could have walked away from. It is a small speech in a small room and it will be repeated on every landing on this river.

choices.label: Hear what happened to him
choices.outcomeText: He was found off the road with the stick still on him. Nobody says your name. Nobody needs to, and no denial you make will travel as far as the story already has.

choices.label: Ask to share the ground
choices.outcomeText: It takes longer to agree than it takes to move in. Both parties keep their weapons where they can reach them and neither party mentions it.

choices.label: Take the shelter
choices.outcomeText: They go out into it because you have more people. You are dry all night, and you spend a good portion of it listening for them.

choices.label: Ride it out in the open
choices.outcomeText: It is a very bad night and it costs you. It also costs you nothing else, ever, which is not a thing you can weigh at the time.

choices.label: Talk
choices.outcomeText: His name is worth remembering and he gives it. He is scouting a corridor his superiors have already decided about, and he is not enthusiastic, and he says so to strangers in the dark.

choices.label: Keep to your own fire
choices.outcomeText: The night passes. Two groups, one overhang, nothing said that either could report.

choices.label: Hear him out
choices.outcomeText: He tells you what is coming up this road behind him and asks for nothing. He is not betraying anyone by his own reckoning, and he has thought about it carefully.

choices.label: Take the warning
choices.outcomeText: He tells you to be off this road by dark and rides on without waiting for a reply. It is not a courtesy. It is a man settling an account cheaply.

choices.label: Recognize him
choices.outcomeText: You have seen this man before, at a small fire on the edge of your own holdings, refusing to give a name. He gives it now. It explains the week he spent watching your border and none of the rest of it.

choices.label: Escort him a stretch
choices.outcomeText: He works the whole way and talks very little, and what you get at the end of it is better than what you were offered at the start.

choices.label: Buy a sheet outright
choices.outcomeText: A clean transaction. He takes payment, hands over a copy, and does not pretend you are now associates.

choices.label: Leave him to his work
choices.outcomeText: He is still setting up the plane table when you are out of sight.

choices.label: Say nothing about it
choices.outcomeText: You use what he sold you and think about what he is selling elsewhere.

choices.label: Ask who else has bought
choices.outcomeText: He tells you. He tells you accurately and without embarrassment, and you understand that he will answer the same question about you.

choices.label: Let him sell it
choices.outcomeText: The sheet goes out. Your fords and your grades are now somebody else's planning material, and the mapmaker will remember that you were reasonable.

choices.label: Buy the exclusive
choices.outcomeText: It costs badly. He hands over the original and the working notes, and the transaction is honest, which you will only be able to confirm much later.

choices.label: Make sure it isn't sold
choices.outcomeText: The sheet does not reach a buyer. Neither does the man. Surveyors are a small profession and they all know each other's routes, and they will notice which route ended where.

choices.label: Mark it and move on
choices.outcomeText: Your mark goes on the frame. Marks are respected by people who intend to respect them.

choices.label: Start cutting
choices.outcomeText: Your unit settles in for slow, unglamorous work, and the first lengths come free by the end of the week.

choices.label: Take it
choices.outcomeText: They break camp because the alternative is worse and everyone present can do the arithmetic. Nobody raises a hand. The windlass stays, because they cannot carry it.

choices.label: Split the wreck
choices.outcomeText: Half the frame and their gear and their labor, which turns out to be the better half of the deal. Their cutting crew is worth three of yours.

choices.label: Leave them the wreck
choices.outcomeText: You pull your people off and take nothing. The oldest man there watches you go and makes a point of learning your colors.

choices.label: Put them to work
choices.outcomeText: They hire on gladly. They are the best cutting crew in the territory and they came to you first.

choices.label: Pass them on the road
choices.outcomeText: They step off the track to let your column through and not one of them looks up. Two settlements on this route will decline to trade with you this season and neither will give a reason.

choices.label: Recognize their foreman
choices.outcomeText: The man running the crew is the one who camped a week on your border and would not give a name. He gives it now, along with the reason he was looking your holdings over: he was deciding whether your people were the kind who take a wreck off families.

choices.label: Answer him
choices.outcomeText: One word back on his band, short enough to be nothing if anyone else is listening. He does not reply, which is correct.

choices.label: Log it and move on
choices.outcomeText: Your officer writes down the band and the time and the fact that no reply was sent. It stays in the log.

choices.label: Ask for him openly
choices.outcomeText: You put it in writing under your own seal, which means they now know precisely what you want and precisely how much you're willing to be seen wanting it.

choices.label: Take him
choices.outcomeText: Your people start looking at the wall the way people look at a wall they intend to be on the other side of.

choices.label: Get him out quietly
choices.outcomeText: Nobody makes a demand and nobody fires a shot, and the whole thing depends on people you have spent a long time paying for.

choices.label: Leave it alone
choices.outcomeText: You move on. Somebody else will hear that band eventually.

choices.label: Press the request
choices.outcomeText: You hold them to it in the open, in front of their own people, and wait for an answer they have to give.

choices.label: Meet their price
choices.outcomeText: It is more than he is worth by any accounting you could defend, and you pay it, and both sides pretend this was a trade.

choices.label: Withdraw the request
choices.outcomeText: You let it go. They will move him within the week, and they will remember that you asked.

choices.label: Go in hard
choices.outcomeText: It is short and loud and it goes the way these things go.

choices.label: Hit the workshop only
choices.outcomeText: A narrow raid on one building instead of a settlement, which is harder to do and much better for him if it works.

choices.label: Run it as planned
choices.outcomeText: Three days of nothing, and then eleven minutes.

choices.label: Buy the gate watch first
choices.outcomeText: Expensive, and it removes the single worst variable in the plan.

choices.label: Tell him he's free to go
choices.outcomeText: He sits with that for a while. Then he says that he has spent four years being valuable to people who did not ask, and that he would like to stay and work for someone who did. He means it, and he will hold you to the standard you just set.

choices.label: Put him to work
choices.outcomeText: He nods once and asks where the bench is. He does not argue and he does not sulk. He simply understands that nothing has changed except the name over the door.

choices.label: Take the guard off the door
choices.outcomeText: He finishes what he is working on, packs the brass set, and is gone inside two days. He tells you where he is going, which he did not have to do.

choices.label: Leave it as it is
choices.outcomeText: The work continues. It is very good work.

choices.label: See to it properly
choices.outcomeText: He is buried well. It changes nothing about what the other wire-readers will hear.

choices.label: Let it stand
choices.outcomeText: You pull back. The band stays quiet for a long time after that.

choices.label: Account for it
choices.outcomeText: There is nothing to do but carry it.

choices.label: Send your wire-reader down
choices.outcomeText: He is down there most of a day with a lamp and a roll of tools, and he comes up filthy and pleased. It was never going to explode, he says, not for anyone who could read the panel — and then he explains what it was for, and the explanation is worth more than the room.

choices.label: Take the wagons
choices.outcomeText: It is over in minutes and the escort never identifies who hit them. Your people are back on their own ground by dark, carrying more than they left with, and there is not one thing in the world to connect it to you.

choices.label: See it safely to Dambar
choices.outcomeText: The escort captain is deeply suspicious for the first two days and stops being so on the third. Your unit rides with them until the road runs out at the high city.

choices.label: Let it pass
choices.outcomeText: You watch six wagons and their thin escort go by below you and you do nothing at all about it.

choices.label: Pay him
choices.outcomeText: He takes it, thanks you, and is a model soldier from that day forward. The matter is closed. You are now a person who can be asked.

choices.label: Refuse him
choices.outcomeText: He does exactly what he said he would do, which at least means he was honest with you. Inside a month the Versari know who was on that road.

choices.label: Hang him in the square
choices.outcomeText: You charge him with something else entirely and hang him in front of the whole garrison. Nobody asks about the road. Nobody asks about anything, afterward.

choices.label: Have it done quietly
choices.outcomeText: He goes missing on a routine patrol and the search is thorough and unsuccessful. Nothing is ever proven and nobody who served with him believes a word of it.

choices.label: Accept their thanks
choices.outcomeText: You take the credit you are owed and leave them their dignity, which they notice.

choices.label: Offer to find out why
choices.outcomeText: You tell them plainly that you trust the Versari no further than they do, and that you have people who can go and look. They do not say yes out loud. They tell you where the granaries are and who counts them.

choices.label: Offer them your own grain
choices.outcomeText: Five loads out of your own stores, given openly, which means the Versari factor in the hall watches it happen and writes it down.

choices.label: Send it
choices.outcomeText: The second shipment is what breaks their dependence, and everyone involved understands exactly what that means. There is a Versari agreement that will not be signed this year because of what you sent.

choices.label: Decline
choices.outcomeText: They thank you for what you already gave, promise not to ask again, and keep that promise.

choices.label: Get him what he needs
choices.outcomeText: It costs a great deal to move that much into a Versari city quietly, and it is in his hands within the week.

choices.label: Tell him to finish it
choices.outcomeText: He acknowledges the order without comment and goes back to work with what he has.

choices.label: Pull him out
choices.outcomeText: You call it off. He argues once, briefly, and then obeys, and he is out of the city inside three days with nothing.

choices.label: Hear them out
choices.outcomeText: They do not blame you and that is somehow the whole problem.

choices.label: Give him the word
choices.outcomeText: He goes for the wall on the second night.

choices.label: Follow the tracks
choices.outcomeText: Heavy wheels and a lot of them, running west and not troubling to hide it.

choices.label: Identify the dead
choices.outcomeText: Your people go through it properly, which takes most of the day and is not pleasant work.

choices.label: Ride on
choices.outcomeText: You leave them where they lie. Somebody will come for them or nobody will.

choices.label: Follow the tracks
choices.outcomeText: You know who they were now, which changes the character of the ride west.

choices.label: Ride on
choices.outcomeText: You carry what you know and do nothing with it, for now.

choices.label: Challenge them for the spoils
choices.outcomeText: You tell him what they took and from whom and what you intend to do about it, and he does not bother denying any part of it.

choices.label: Threaten to tell the Goldgrass
choices.outcomeText: You tell him exactly how far this wall is from the nearest Goldgrass hall and how quickly that can be corrected. He stops smiling and reaches for the horn.

choices.label: Leave — you know where they are
choices.outcomeText: You turn around in full view and ride out, and every man on that rampart understands that the location is now worth something to somebody.

choices.label: Hand over what you took
choices.outcomeText: You put the recovered goods on their table and take nothing for it. The hall goes quiet. That is not a thing outsiders do here.

choices.label: Keep it and tell them anyway
choices.outcomeText: You give them the location and say nothing about the rest. They are grateful for the one and will learn about the other eventually.

choices.label: Ride back with them
choices.outcomeText: They ask, in the manner of people who have already decided to go with or without you. You say yes.

choices.label: Leave it with them
choices.outcomeText: You have told them what you know. What they do about it is theirs.

choices.label: Take the wall
choices.outcomeText: It is a long morning and the wall was better than it looked.

choices.label: Hear him out
choices.outcomeText: You give him the room and the hour he asked for.

choices.label: Send him away
choices.outcomeText: He is gone before midday without having said his piece, and Clan Tempest will hear the manner of it before he is home.

choices.label: Offer him your soldiers
choices.outcomeText: You commit to the field. He does not thank you extravagantly; among Lakers, that would suggest he had doubted you.

choices.label: Offer material support
choices.outcomeText: Twelve loads, paid out over the campaign. He accepts it as what it is, and files away what it isn't.

choices.label: Refuse him
choices.outcomeText: You turn down a war and a clan in the same sentence. He leaves without discourtesy and Tempest will remember this for a generation.

choices.label: Warn the Lakers
choices.outcomeText: You send everything he told you to the coalition, in detail, while he is still riding home.

choices.label: Commit units to the siege
choices.outcomeText: Your columns go in on the northern works alongside Tempest's.

choices.label: Send nothing
choices.outcomeText: You let the call go unanswered. They notice immediately and say nothing until it is over.

choices.label: Settle accounts
choices.outcomeText: Tempest is precise about what it owes and equally precise about what it doesn't.

choices.label: Take the payment
choices.outcomeText: You take it. It is not very much and it was never going to be.

choices.label: Ride down to them
choices.outcomeText: You go in openly, which under most circumstances is the correct thing to do.

choices.label: Watch from the ridge
choices.outcomeText: Your scouts get up on the high ground and put glasses on the hollow without ever breaking the skyline.

choices.label: Leave them to it
choices.outcomeText: Whatever it is, it is theirs. You ride wide of the hollow and keep going.

choices.label: Ask what they need
choices.outcomeText: The anger goes out of them the moment you ask. What they need, it turns out, they have needed for two years.

choices.label: Break out
choices.outcomeText: They are farmers with hand tools and they close anyway, which is worse to remember than a real fight would have been.

choices.label: Go down and offer help
choices.outcomeText: You wait for the rite to finish, come in slowly and in the open, and are received as guests.

choices.label: Go through the wagons
choices.outcomeText: Two of your people are in and out while the singing is still going. It is the easiest thing you have done all season.

choices.label: Leave them undisturbed
choices.outcomeText: You pull back off the ridge before the rite ends and they never know anyone was there.

choices.label: Take it from him
choices.outcomeText: The estate is held better than any farmhouse has a right to be.

choices.label: Hear his price
choices.outcomeText: He wants your unit. Not forever — a season, for something he has coming up and would rather not use his own name on. The relic is yours when they come back.

choices.label: Withdraw
choices.outcomeText: You leave the Baron his prize and the Croppers their disappointment.

choices.label: Return it to the Croppers
choices.outcomeText: You put it back in the hands it came from and refuse what they try to give you for it. That story will be told in every plains hollow between here and the river within a year.

choices.label: Give it to the Goldgrass
choices.outcomeText: The factor pays well and immediately, and the Goldgrass halls are openly pleased. Somewhere a hollow full of farmers finds out secondhand.

choices.label: Gift it to the Free Plainers
choices.outcomeText: You hand a Goldgrass treasure to the Free Plainers as an open gesture, which is a thing only a Goldgrass power could do and have it read as generosity rather than insult.

choices.label: Answer for it
choices.outcomeText: You explain the arrangement to people who have already decided what it was. It does not help.

choices.label: Add your own names
choices.outcomeText: Your people take turns at it and take it more seriously than any of them would admit to.

choices.label: Rest in the shade
choices.outcomeText: An hour out of the sun in the coolest place for forty miles. Nobody says much.

choices.label: Ride on
choices.outcomeText: You leave it standing behind you and it takes most of the afternoon to go out of sight.

choices.label: Sign his book and cross
choices.outcomeText: He writes the obligation in a clean hand, turns the ledger for you to see it, and waves you across without ceremony.

choices.label: Take the long way
choices.outcomeText: Two extra fords and a great deal of broken ground. Your column arrives tired and owing nobody anything.

choices.label: Have her read the road
choices.outcomeText: She takes the fee, sits with it a while, and describes what is ahead in plain language with the uncertain parts marked as uncertain.

choices.label: Pass by
choices.outcomeText: You go on through. The queue closes up behind you without anyone looking round.

choices.label: Go aboard
choices.outcomeText: They show you round without much interest. Someone's grandmother sleeps where the drive housing used to be.

choices.label: Ride on
choices.outcomeText: Your engineer looks back at it twice on the way out of town.

choices.label: Wait with him
choices.outcomeText: You lose the afternoon. Toward dark the river comes up nine inches for no reason anyone can point at, and he does not say anything about it.

choices.label: Cross anyway
choices.outcomeText: You cross without incident and he watches every yard of it and still does not move.

choices.label: Find another crossing
choices.outcomeText: There is one, four miles up, and it costs you the rest of the day.

choices.label: Ask what they mean
choices.outcomeText: He talks for an hour and would happily have gone longer.

choices.label: Leave him to his road
choices.outcomeText: He nods and walks on, sleeves still rolled.

choices.label: Ask about the notes
choices.outcomeText: He explains the system with total confidence and gets at least one part of it wrong.

choices.label: Trade and move on
choices.outcomeText: You do business and go.

choices.label: Let her talk
choices.outcomeText: She goes on for a long time and her dates never once slip.

choices.label: Excuse yourself
choices.outcomeText: She is still talking when your column pulls out.

choices.label: Hear him out
choices.outcomeText: You learn a great deal about Laker pig iron that you did not ask to learn.

choices.label: See him down the road
choices.outcomeText: He does not understand that anything was done for him, which is the best outcome available.

choices.label: Ride on
choices.outcomeText: He waves. He is still waving when you look back.

choices.label: Call again
choices.outcomeText: Nothing. The figure at the window does not move and does not leave.

choices.label: Keep riding
choices.outcomeText: You pass within fifty yards of a working farm and are not acknowledged by anyone on it.

choices.label: Attend
choices.outcomeText: You stand at the back. The grandmother is enormously pleased and does not say so.

choices.label: Send word instead
choices.outcomeText: A message and nothing more, which is entirely adequate and noticed anyway.

choices.label: Settle it
choices.outcomeText: You rule. They accept it immediately, and within a month they have found a different coil to argue about.

choices.label: Leave them to it
choices.outcomeText: You back out of the workshop. It is still going when you reach the end of the street.

choices.label: Go out to the field
choices.outcomeText: You stand at the edge and it is over in an hour and nobody makes anything of your being there.

choices.label: Let them have it
choices.outcomeText: The singing carries as far as the hall and stops at about the hour they said it would.

choices.label: Ask your steward about it
choices.outcomeText: He gives you both explanations and declines to choose between them.

choices.label: Think nothing of it
choices.outcomeText: You forget about it entirely until the next time somebody does it.

choices.label: Take her counsel in the open
choices.outcomeText: You sit with her in the hall with the doors open. What she says is careful, specific, and marked where she is unsure. Everyone in the settlement knows by nightfall that this seat listens.

choices.label: Take her counsel privately
choices.outcomeText: You hear her alone. You get the same counsel and none of the standing, which may be exactly what you wanted.

choices.label: Turn her away
choices.outcomeText: She takes it without offence and is on the road before midday. Your settlement has opinions about it that nobody brings to you.

choices.label: Pay her to say what you've decided
choices.outcomeText: She looks at you for a while and then does it, word for word, in the open hall. She leaves the same evening without collecting the rest of the fee.

choices.label: Hang him
choices.outcomeText: It is done at the wall in the morning. If somebody sent him, they will hear about it. If nobody sent him, nobody will ever hear about it at all.

choices.label: Hold him and keep asking
choices.outcomeText: Weeks of it. Eventually there is a story — a name, a place, a reason — and it holds together well enough to be true and well enough to have been built. You are no more certain than you were on the first day.

choices.label: Turn him loose
choices.outcomeText: He walks out the way he came in, with everything he saw on the way through, and thanks nobody.

choices.label: Give it to your kin
choices.outcomeText: He is grateful, competent enough, and entirely loyal. The stores are in the hands of family now, which is a thing your settlement understands perfectly well.

choices.label: Take a chance on the woman
choices.outcomeText: She is startled to be asked and accepts before she can talk herself out of it. Nobody in the settlement can tell you whether this will work.

choices.label: Hire someone who's done it
choices.outcomeText: He arrives inside a month, reorganises everything in a fortnight, and is disliked immediately and universally.

choices.label: Let the block stand
choices.outcomeText: You accept the objection publicly. The agreement dies and the seat becomes real in the same afternoon.

choices.label: Work them
choices.outcomeText: You spend three days in a room with them and get most of what you wanted. It costs you three days.

choices.label: Comply
choices.outcomeText: You take the loss. It is a real loss and everybody watching understands that you took it because you said you would.

choices.label: Override them
choices.outcomeText: It takes an afternoon and nobody physically stops you. The seat still exists. Everyone now knows exactly what it is.

choices.label: See how they deal with you now
choices.outcomeText: The envoys have adjusted. They are not being rude about it.

choices.label: Put him to work
choices.outcomeText: He starts the same week and is better than the work requires.

choices.label: Send him on
choices.outcomeText: He takes it evenly, thanks you for the time, and finds work two streets over within a day.

choices.label: Leave it alone
choices.outcomeText: The quarter runs better than it has in years, through a man who holds no post at all.

choices.label: Back your appointee
choices.outcomeText: You make the chain of authority explicit. It is obeyed and it is not believed.

choices.label: Give him the post
choices.outcomeText: You formalise what the quarter already decided. He is good at it for a long time.

choices.label: Refuse him
choices.outcomeText: You say no to the most capable person available, for reasons you could defend and would rather not have to.

choices.label: Acknowledge the notice
choices.outcomeText: You send back that you heard them. There is nothing else to send.

choices.label: Grant the passage
choices.outcomeText: It crosses your ground on their timetable and you host what you would rather not host, and the debt is paid in full and in public.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.outcomeText: You tell them no. They do not argue and they do not ask again, and the grain they sent you three winters ago becomes a thing that is mentioned.

choices.label: Offer something else
choices.outcomeText: You substitute material for permission. They accept it because refusing would be graceless, and both sides know the substitution was not equal.

choices.label: Close the book
choices.outcomeText: The obligation is discharged. What it left behind is not.

choices.label: Give him what he asked for
choices.outcomeText: He takes the materials and the room and thanks you once, briefly, and is not seen much for a month.

choices.label: Turn him down
choices.outcomeText: He accepts it without complaint and goes back to work. He does not ask again.

choices.label: Leave him to it
choices.outcomeText: You tell the reporter it isn't a problem, which is true and does not entirely settle them.

choices.label: Ask him directly
choices.outcomeText: You go to the room and ask. He puts down what he is holding and answers.

choices.label: Help him finish it
choices.outcomeText: You give him the height he needs and the parts he cannot make, and a month later something answers him from a very long way off.

choices.label: Tell him to stop
choices.outcomeText: He stops. He does not argue and he does not dismantle it, and the list stays in the drawer.

choices.label: Follow it back
choices.outcomeText: Quietly, and through the old books, which takes weeks and nobody notices you doing it.

choices.label: Let it lie
choices.outcomeText: It is small enough to absorb and old enough to be somebody else's fault. You absorb it.

choices.label: Bring them in
choices.outcomeText: You put the ledgers on the table and wait. They do not pretend for very long.

choices.label: Make an example
choices.outcomeText: You do it publicly after all. The stores will not be short again for a long time and the third quarter will not forget how it was done.

choices.label: Settle it in the room
choices.outcomeText: Restitution, a demotion, and no announcement. Four people know. It holds.

choices.label: Bury it
choices.outcomeText: The books are corrected, the shortfall is written off against the dead man, and nothing else happens at all.

choices.label: Note that she was right
choices.outcomeText: You say so, once, where people can hear it. That is all it takes.

choices.label: Say nothing about it
choices.outcomeText: You let it pass without comment. The settlement makes the connection anyway.

choices.label: Give her a place at the hall
choices.outcomeText: You make it official, which she did not want and cannot now refuse.

choices.label: Leave it informal
choices.outcomeText: No post, no title, and a queue outside her door every morning regardless.

choices.label: Accept it in front of them
choices.outcomeText: You change course in the open, on the word of a woman with no post and no army, and the hall watches you do it.

choices.label: Proceed anyway
choices.outcomeText: You thank her for her counsel and do the thing regardless, and every person in the room now knows the precise value of being asked.

choices.label: Follow the line
choices.outcomeText: It takes the better part of a day and the stones keep coming, spaced by somebody who knew exactly how far a person walks between them.

choices.label: Mark it and move on
choices.outcomeText: You put the junction on your own map and leave the stones standing.

choices.label: Wait and see who comes
choices.outcomeText: You plant your unit and sit through the afternoon. The handoff happens in front of you because there is no longer any way for it not to, and you learn what this line carries and who it carries it for. They know precisely what you now know.

choices.label: Hold the site and receive it
choices.outcomeText: Your people take the ground and stand in it as though they belong there, and what arrives is handed over before anyone works out that it shouldn't have been. The line will not run through here again.

choices.label: Trade on what you know
choices.outcomeText: You tell them plainly that you can read every stone between here and wherever this starts, and that you would rather have an arrangement than a haul. They are carriers, not fighters. An arrangement is worth far more to them than this one meeting.

choices.label: Break the stones on the way out
choices.outcomeText: Eleven junctions, a hammer, and half a day. The line dies. Nobody ever finds out it was you, and something that had been working for years stops working.

choices.label: Look closer
choices.outcomeText: Adults, all three, buried with care and in a hurry, which are not usually the same thing.

choices.label: Leave them
choices.outcomeText: You ride out of the yard and the graves go behind you.

choices.label: Ask them what happened
choices.outcomeText: They tell you what they can, which is a sequence of events with the middle missing. Three people were well and then they were not and there was nothing between the two states that anyone can describe.

choices.label: Ask them what happened
choices.outcomeText: Their account has a detail in it that you have heard before, from a family on a different road who could not have spoken to these people. Neither family thought the detail was important. You are the only person alive who has heard both.

choices.label: See them safely north
choices.outcomeText: A day out of your way. They do not say much and they do not stop looking behind them.

choices.label: Let them go
choices.outcomeText: They are moving again before your column is.

choices.label: Take the letter and read it
choices.outcomeText: You break a seal that was not yours and put it back badly, and the boy watches you do it and says nothing.

choices.label: See him down the road
choices.outcomeText: You ride the bad stretch with him and hand him off at the far end. He tells you his name without being asked.

choices.label: Let him by
choices.outcomeText: He is gone at a canter inside a minute.

choices.label: Ask who's paying him now
choices.outcomeText: He tells you cheerfully and in detail, because you rode a bad stretch with him once and he has never forgotten it. What he tells you is that the correspondence has changed hands.

choices.label: Press him
choices.outcomeText: He is careful with you, gives you the minimum, and rides on early. You get the name and nothing around it.

choices.label: Let him by again
choices.outcomeText: The same road, the same speed, a different seal.

choices.label: Ride the dark stretch with him
choices.outcomeText: Six hours at a walking pace. He talks the whole way and most of it is useful.

choices.label: Leave him to it
choices.outcomeText: His lamp goes on down the road and out of sight.

choices.label: Take what he's carrying
choices.outcomeText: He hands it over, visibly lighter for it, and is gone before you have finished thinking about what to do with it.

choices.label: Note it and leave it
choices.outcomeText: You leave the blind exactly as you found it, down to the brush across the entrance.

choices.label: Pull it apart now
choices.outcomeText: Twenty minutes and it is a pile of cut brush. Whoever built it will know within days that somebody objected.

choices.label: Take the tally
choices.outcomeText: Four months of crossings in a careful hand — who, how many, which direction, what they were hauling. He does not try to stop you. Whoever commissioned this will notice the gap.

choices.label: Leave it and change the numbers
choices.outcomeText: You add crossings that never happened and take out several that did, and put the board back on its peg. He watches you do it and understands immediately that his position has improved. Whoever reads this count will act on your arithmetic.

choices.label: Buy him
choices.outcomeText: One payment, settled on the spot, worth more than the season he was promised. He keeps counting for them and sends you a copy of everything, and this ford does not go dark to you again.

choices.label: Burn it
choices.outcomeText: He is out of it and well up the bank before it catches. Nobody counts anything at this crossing after today, and the owner learns that much within the week.

choices.label: Hear him out
choices.outcomeText: He states his case briefly and without pressure, which is itself a kind of pressure. He has done this before.

choices.label: Tell him to leave
choices.outcomeText: He goes without argument and without hurry, and he stops at the works on his way out of the settlement to say something brief to the boy that nobody else hears.

choices.label: Tell them to let him go
choices.outcomeText: The mother cries and agrees and thanks you for it, which will be difficult to think about later. He is packed and gone inside two days.

choices.label: Advise against it, quietly
choices.outcomeText: You give them reasons in a private room and they take the advice. Nothing is announced and nobody is forbidden anything, and the boy knows exactly where the decision was made.

choices.label: Forbid it
choices.outcomeText: You say no where it can be heard, and the reason you give is the settlement's need, which is true and is not the whole truth. The scholar accepts it immediately. He has been refused before and expected it here.

choices.label: Demand terms
choices.outcomeText: A set span, and the boy comes back. There is nothing to sign and no one to enforce it — the scholar's word is the only instrument that exists. He agrees at once, which is not as reassuring as it should be.

choices.label: Carry on without him
choices.outcomeText: The works adapts. It adapts downward.

choices.label: Leave him to it
choices.outcomeText: You keep a capable man and get the work of an ordinary one, which is the exact shape of what you chose.

choices.label: Speak to him yourself
choices.outcomeText: He is respectful throughout and gives you nothing. He is not going to argue with the seat that decided his life, and he is not going to forget which seat it was.

choices.label: Put him to work
choices.outcomeText: He is worth what he cost. What he brought back with him is a separate account, and it has not been settled.

choices.label: Send the second scholar away
choices.outcomeText: You put the older man on the road inside the week. He is not offended and does not hurry, and he has already seen the works.

choices.label: Take the advance
choices.outcomeText: He writes the entry, turns the book so you can see it written, and has the wagon unloaded before the ink is dry.

choices.label: Decline
choices.outcomeText: He closes the book without any change of expression, thanks you for the hearing, and is on the road within the hour. He does not say he will return.

choices.label: Take the second advance
choices.outcomeText: The second entry goes under the first on the same page. He mentions, without emphasis, that the settlement is now among his better accounts.

choices.label: Decline this one
choices.outcomeText: He accepts it without argument and does not try to talk you round, which is somehow more unsettling than if he had.

choices.label: Pay it in full
choices.outcomeText: It empties the stores and it takes three days to load. He signs the entry closed, writes something short beside it that you cannot read upside down, and shakes your hand.

choices.label: Pay what you can
choices.outcomeText: He takes it, credits it accurately, and re-enters the remainder at a rate that reflects the delay. He is not punishing you. This is simply what the book does with an unpaid balance.

choices.label: Refuse to pay
choices.outcomeText: There is no argument and no threat. He rules a line under both entries, writes one word at the end of it, and leaves. Within two months no Versari factor within four hundred miles will unload a wagon at your gate, and none of them will ever say why.

choices.label: Say nothing about it
choices.outcomeText: You keep it to yourself. It is the single most valuable thing anyone in your settlement saw this year and you cannot do one thing with it.

choices.label: Tell the other settlements
choices.outcomeText: You send word to every hall your riders can reach. Most of them already suspected. A few of them stop borrowing. The Versari find out who told them inside a season.

choices.label: Take the share
choices.outcomeText: You accept her arrangement, which is generous by her reckoning and costs her nothing she was going to keep. Neither of you uses the word permission.

choices.label: Charge them rent
choices.outcomeText: She is baffled by the concept, argues it briefly on the merits, and then pays — in stock rather than scrap, at a rate she sets. You have established a principle and not much else.

choices.label: Order them off the field
choices.outcomeText: Forty people and no footing worth arguing over. They are gone in three days without a word of complaint, and the iron goes back to lying where it has lain for a century.

choices.label: Meet what they need
choices.outcomeText: Hands, food and passage east, paid every season without fail, and in return your works get material they could not otherwise have touched.

choices.label: Trade for goods only
choices.outcomeText: You pay in kind and refuse the passage clause. She accepts it and the hauls go east anyway, by a route nobody discusses with you.

choices.label: Refuse the arrangement
choices.outcomeText: She shrugs and sells the run to somebody else within the month. The works does not slow down at all.

choices.label: Formalize it on your terms
choices.outcomeText: Weeks of negotiation with a foundry foreman who turns out to be a considerably better negotiator than anyone you employ.

choices.label: Force them out
choices.outcomeText: It is still possible. It will not be possible in another year and everyone involved knows it, which is why it happens now and why it happens badly.

choices.label: Leave it alone
choices.outcomeText: You make no decision at all, which is a decision, and the works takes it as one.

choices.label: Sign it
choices.outcomeText: The stacks keep running and the output is yours on paper.

choices.label: Let them go
choices.outcomeText: The road east is busy for a week and then it is not.

choices.label: Leave it as it stands
choices.outcomeText: Nothing is settled. Everything works.

choices.label: Let them pass
choices.outcomeText: It is out of sight in under a minute and your people talk about it for a week.

choices.label: Hail them
choices.outcomeText: They stop, briefly. The driver answers three questions about the build with real enthusiasm and every question about their route with none at all.

choices.label: Offer them your yard
choices.outcomeText: You give them space, a forge and a roof. They accept immediately and are working within the hour, and the work does not solve their problem.

choices.label: Leave them to it
choices.outcomeText: They make camp at the road edge and start pulling the quarter apart to see how bad it is. It is bad.

choices.label: Sell them the shell
choices.outcomeText: They pay well and without haggling, which tells you afterward that you could have asked for more. It is on their flatbed and going east inside three days.

choices.label: Trade it for the work
choices.outcomeText: Not scrap. A fabricator, on your ground, for a season, building in the open where your people can watch every cut. He argues the length of it and not the principle, and settles at a season.

choices.label: Say nothing about it
choices.outcomeText: You let them go home on the tow. The shell stays in the rubble field, and every one of your people who knows it is there now also knows what it was worth.

choices.label: Assign it to a unit
choices.outcomeText: It goes to whoever needs to be somewhere fast, and everyone who sees it on the road knows precisely what it is and roughly what it cost you.

choices.label: Take the trade
choices.outcomeText: You let it run. Your people are better off by Friday than they were on Monday and there is nothing in that you can bring yourself to object to.

choices.label: Tax it first
choices.outcomeText: You set a levy on the table before you let it open. Brey does not argue, does not appeal, and does not appear to mind; he recalculates his prices in front of you, faster than your steward can follow, and the line forms anyway. You have taken a cut of something you do not yet understand the shape of.

choices.label: Turn him out
choices.outcomeText: He packs the table without complaint and is gone before dark. Your people do not say anything to you about it, which is how you learn how much they wanted those prices.

choices.label: Let him keep them in notes
choices.outcomeText: The friction stops that week. So does any real sense of what your own granary is worth in anything except a number printed three hundred miles east.

choices.label: Forbid it
choices.outcomeText: The order is obeyed and the cost goes on being paid, out of your stores, every week, by a man who told you it would.

choices.label: Issue your own tally against their reserve
choices.outcomeText: It costs more to set up than anyone tells you it will, and for two months it is plainly worse than either alternative. Then it is not. Your steward's columns reconcile against something with your name on it.

choices.label: Give her the pledge
choices.outcomeText: You put your grain land under somebody else's plan for it and you are paid handsomely, immediately, and in a currency you do not print.

choices.label: Refuse the pledge
choices.outcomeText: She is not offended, and she does not threaten you, and the credit simply does not open. Brey stays. The prices stay. Nothing bad happens, which is its own kind of answer.

choices.label: Take the credit and keep your options
choices.outcomeText: You give the pledge, take the money, and put a third of the pledged ground under something that is not grain before the season turns. It is the correct decision and you would rather it had been made by somebody else.

choices.label: Let it stand
choices.outcomeText: It works. It goes on working. That is the whole of it.

choices.label: Take the loss
choices.outcomeText: You had the money and the ground and the season, and now you have the ground and the season, and everyone here watched it happen.

choices.label: Put your tally behind it
choices.outcomeText: The thing you paid for two seasons ago turns out to be the thing you needed. Your notes are not better than theirs. They are simply not theirs.

choices.label: Go back to barter
choices.outcomeText: It is slower and poorer and entirely your own, and your steward pays the friction out of the stores every week without being asked to, the way he did before any of this started.

choices.label: Enforce the contract
choices.outcomeText: The Croppers are in the field on the fourteenth because you put them there, and they cut well, because they are good at it and because it would not occur to them to do it badly. Nobody sings. Your grain is in before the weather and you are the one who spent their hour.

choices.label: Let the rite stand
choices.outcomeText: The hollow gets its day. The cut starts on the fifteenth into a sky that has already made up its mind, and what comes out of that field is meaningfully less than what was standing in it. Chelle's ledger does not record a loss, because there was not one — not on his side of it.

choices.label: Buy the contract out
choices.outcomeText: You pay the hall to release its claim on your own harvest, which is a strange sentence to say aloud and an expensive one to act on. But the schedule is yours now, the Croppers cut on the fifteenth and sing on the fourteenth, and you have taken a permanent arrangement out of somebody else's hands.

choices.label: Tell them to settle it between themselves
choices.outcomeText: You decline to be the one who says which day matters. Chelle settles it in an afternoon, without you, by the only instrument he has — he offers the Croppers more notes to cut on the fourteenth, and they take it, and something between them is worse afterward in a way that neither of them will name. Your grain comes in. The arrangement you inherited is now his.

choices.label: Cut it with your own people
choices.outcomeText: Your soldiers bring in a harvest badly and slowly and most of it survives the doing. Fisk watches from the headland the entire time, without comment, which your people find harder than shouting.

choices.label: Let it stand
choices.outcomeText: The weather arrives on schedule and takes most of what was in that field. Nobody is at fault in a way you could write down, which does not make the granary any less empty.

choices.label: Ask them to name a second hour
choices.outcomeText: Fisk names one before you have finished the question. There has always been a second hour. It is later and lesser and permitted, and in forty years of contracts and factors and schedules, nobody has ever asked her for it.

choices.label: Take them on
choices.outcomeText: They come onto your ground as your people, which they have views about and accept anyway, because the alternative is worse and because Fisk tells them to. They are the best harvest labor on the continent and you now have all of it.

choices.label: Move them along
choices.outcomeText: They go west, because west is where people go who have stopped being anybody's business, and the Free Plainers take them in without asking a single question about it. Fisk does not say goodbye to you. There is no reason she should.

choices.label: Press the hall to restore the rate
choices.outcomeText: It takes a season, a great deal of money, and the surrender of every advantage you were holding, and at the end of it the rate is restored and the schedule reads the way it read before. Chelle is professionally impressed and personally unbothered.

choices.label: Keep the hour
choices.outcomeText: It costs you a day a year. It is the cheapest thing you have ever bought.

choices.label: Let them go
choices.outcomeText: One fewer people on your ground, one more people in somebody else's column, and a harvest you will be hiring at market rates from now on.

choices.label: Stand as guarantor
choices.outcomeText: You are now the third name on an agreement between two peoples who managed without one for forty years. It will hold as long as you do.

choices.label: Hear her terms
choices.outcomeText: She names a figure that is most of what the village has and does not pretend otherwise.

choices.label: Decline
choices.outcomeText: She thanks you for coming out to say so, which she did not have to do. Three rounds later the village is hit, and she does not blame you, and word gets round that she didn't.

choices.label: Meet them in the open
choices.outcomeText: You put yourself between the band and the village on ground you picked, in daylight, where there is no question about who is there and why.

choices.label: Set a trap at the ford
choices.outcomeText: The pattern says the ford and the pattern has been right four times. You are in the willows before dark.

choices.label: Buy them off
choices.outcomeText: You pay Sull more than the village's surplus is worth to go and be a problem somewhere else. He takes it, honors it exactly, and is entirely straightforward about the fact that he will be back when it runs out.

choices.label: Take her fund and ride to Sull instead
choices.outcomeText: You are already being paid to be on this ground and there is a second party who will pay more for the same afternoon's work. Sull finds the arrangement funny in a way you do not enjoy being on the inside of.

choices.label: Take the fund
choices.outcomeText: The band breaks and does not re-form on this stretch. Dorn pays the whole sum without being asked and the hall, which did not send anyone, hears about it within the month. The ground you hold does not get raided, and that is now a thing people say.

choices.label: Take what she offers anyway
choices.outcomeText: The village is stripped. Dorn pays you the full fund regardless, because that was the agreement and because she is that sort of person, and watching her count it out is worse than the fight was.

choices.label: Say nothing about the arrangement
choices.outcomeText: The village is not raided this season and Dorn is grateful in a wholehearted way that would be easier to take if she knew what she was thanking you for. Sull is somebody else's problem until autumn.

choices.label: Ride out past her
choices.outcomeText: She is at the gate post when your column comes back through and she looks at it long enough to count it. She survives. She knows exactly who she hired and she tells everyone, in order, starting with the hall.

choices.label: Take the second job
choices.outcomeText: It pays what he said it would. It goes the way the first one went, under colors that are yours this time as well, and the difference between being used once and being his instrument is a difference you have now stopped being able to argue.

choices.label: Refuse him
choices.outcomeText: The rider takes it back without comment. Within a month the story of the first arrangement is circulating in a version Juan has told himself, in which you were a willing party who has since got cold feet, and there is no version of the truth you can put against it that does not sound exactly like a man with cold feet.

choices.label: Refuse, and go to Colonel Ives first
choices.outcomeText: You send the rider back with nothing and go west the same week, to the leader he hit, before he can decide what version of you she hears.

choices.label: Give her the account
choices.outcomeText: You tell it straight, including the parts that make you look like a man who rented out his own name and did not ask enough questions. She listens the whole way through without interrupting once, and at the end of it she believes you, which is not the same as forgiving you and is worth considerably more.

choices.label: Give her the account and the estate's layout
choices.outcomeText: You saw that estate from the inside when your people were quartered in it. She has the walls, the gate, the well and the number of men on it before you have finished your second cup. Nothing you have done since the arrangement is as clearly a betrayal as this and nothing you have done has been as useful to anyone.

choices.label: Say nothing useful
choices.outcomeText: You go all that way to protect a man you do not like from a woman you have no quarrel with, and you are not even sure, riding back, which loyalty you thought you were honoring. Ives thanks you for coming. Nothing is repaired.

choices.label: Let it finish
choices.outcomeText: Ives takes the estate in a night with fewer people than it should have needed, which tells you what she was given and by whom. Juan does not come out of it. Your name is attached to the thing that ended him and the Plainers are clear-eyed about the fact that it was also your name that let him start.

choices.label: Let the account stand
choices.outcomeText: Juan goes to ground somewhere south with most of his men and none of his standing, which out here is the more permanent of the two losses. The story that circulates is the one you told Ives, because she is the one telling it.

choices.label: Take what comes of it
choices.outcomeText: Juan does very well. He has a second estate by autumn and a version of the last two years in which you were his partner throughout, and there is no longer anybody with an interest in contradicting it. He sends word again in a season. He will keep sending word.

choices.label: Agree terms with Odell
choices.outcomeText: You pay what was agreed and it is a fair price for the ground. Odell begins moving his families the following week, which is when you find out how much of this ground was ever his to move people off.

choices.label: Ask him what he actually speaks for
choices.outcomeText: It is an insulting question and he answers it anyway, in full, because it is the first time anybody from a state has asked it instead of assuming. He speaks for sixty families. There are two other people on this ground and neither of them has ever agreed to anything with him or with each other.

choices.label: Leave the ground alone
choices.outcomeText: There are other hexes and fewer complications on most of them. Odell is puzzled by the withdrawal and slightly insulted, which is the first thing all day that he and the other two claimants would have agreed on.

choices.label: Pay her as well
choices.outcomeText: You buy the same ground twice and she is satisfied, and Odell is humiliated in front of his own people by a transaction he was not part of, and you notice — too late to be useful — how quickly word of a man who pays travels across open country.

choices.label: Hold Odell to his terms
choices.outcomeText: You stand on the agreement, which is a real agreement, made in good faith, by a man who meant it. Odell backs you and cannot enforce a word of it, and standing behind him in front of Ansel's forty riders is the moment you understand that you have not bought ground, you have bought a man's opinion about ground.

choices.label: Ask who else is coming
choices.outcomeText: Ansel laughs. Odell answers, because you asked him the same question a week ago and he has been thinking about it since. There is one more. There is always one more, and the next one is the one who actually lives here.

choices.label: Pay him too
choices.outcomeText: Three payments for one hex, and it holds, and it will go on holding right up until the fourth claimant hears what this ground goes for. You have not established a title. You have established a rate.

choices.label: Back one of them into an authority the others won't grant
choices.outcomeText: You pick one, arm him, and underwrite him until the other two find it cheaper to acknowledge him than to argue. It is the invention of a government by a foreign power on a Tuesday afternoon, and whether it survives you depends entirely on how you are known to rule elsewhere.

choices.label: Take the ground
choices.outcomeText: It takes an afternoon. There is no one to appeal to, no body that can call it illegal, and no mechanism anywhere on this continent by which sixty families and forty riders and eleven years of work can be made into a claim that outlasts the person holding the ground. That is not a flaw in your conduct. It is a flaw in theirs, and it is the whole of their future.

choices.label: Hold it on their goodwill
choices.outcomeText: It works, expensively, for as long as everyone continues to feel about it the way they feel about it today.

choices.label: Let your reputation carry it
choices.outcomeText: You are known for rulings people do not enjoy and do not test twice, and that is precisely what makes the arrangement hold: nobody on this ground believes you would fail to enforce it. The client stands. So does the resentment underneath him.

choices.label: Let it stand on its merits
choices.outcomeText: You are known for rulings that go the way the weaker party hoped, and on this ground that reads as a man who will not come back to enforce anything. Within a season the other two are testing it, politely at first.

choices.label: Hold it
choices.outcomeText: Nobody comes. There is no one whose job it would be.

choices.label: Hire the ring
choices.outcomeText: They are good. They are on time, they do not lose loads, and they cost you a third of what the halls were charging. Your quartermaster is happier than he has been in two seasons.

choices.label: Refuse the rate
choices.outcomeText: Ledger notes it without argument, thanks you for coming, and returns to his accounts before you are out of the yard. You go on paying hall rates, which are honest and which you can afford and which you now know the precise size of.

choices.label: Keep buying
choices.outcomeText: The rate is the rate and the stock is the stock and you have a district to supply. Ledger does not thank you for your discretion, because it has not occurred to him that discretion was involved.

choices.label: Stop
choices.outcomeText: You end the arrangement without explaining why, which Ledger finds mildly inefficient and does not contest. Your costs go back up the following week.

choices.label: Keep buying, and tell the Goldgrass where it came from
choices.outcomeText: You go on taking the rate and you send the hall a full account of the stock and the dates and the yard's location, and you let those two facts sit in the same season without looking at them together for very long.

choices.label: Renew the arrangement
choices.outcomeText: The account is in good order and the rate holds for another season. Somewhere in that ledger, in the correct column, is what those people's chain and axles came to, and it is a smaller number than you had braced for, which is the part that stays with you.

choices.label: Let the account close
choices.outcomeText: He closes it cleanly, with a final statement and no rancor whatsoever, and that is the thing you cannot get past: not that he did it, but that he was never at any point pretending it was something else. You were the only person in the arrangement who needed it to be.

choices.label: Take the rate and read the hall's reply
choices.outcomeText: The hall's answer arrives the same week as Ledger's invoice. It thanks you at some length. It does not say what the hall intends to do, and the rate on your next load is unchanged, and both of those facts are going to be true for exactly as long as they are.

choices.label: Take a sample
choices.outcomeText: It takes most of an afternoon and two ruined chisels to get a piece the size of a thumb, and the fracture face is as flat as the surface. The family watch the entire operation with the patience of people who have seen it tried.

choices.label: Ask them what they know
choices.outcomeText: They know a great deal, in the way people know a field they have lived beside for eleven years: where it stays coldest, which month the frost sits on it and which month it will not, that a dropped tool skitters and does not chip it. None of it explains anything. All of it is worth having.

choices.label: Ride around it
choices.outcomeText: You lose half a day to the detour and your people talk about it for a week, which is more than they would have done if you had stopped.

choices.label: Have it studied anyway
choices.outcomeText: Your people learn nothing about what made it and a surprising amount about what it will and will not do, which is the only kind of knowledge available about anything from before.

choices.label: Leave the family to it
choices.outcomeText: You post nothing, claim nothing and record the location in your own hand. The goats are the only enterprise anybody has ever successfully run on that ground.

choices.label: Hire her honestly
choices.outcomeText: The rate is enormous and she is worth it, and the transaction is conducted entirely between you and the men holding her contract, with her standing there listening to it.

choices.label: Ask what the escort costs her
choices.outcomeText: Nobody has asked her that either. It is most of what she earns, every season, paid to men hired by other people to make sure she arrives — a protection she did not commission and cannot decline, because the moment she travels alone she is worth taking.

choices.label: Take her
choices.outcomeText: Four men is not many. It is done before the road is clear and she does not resist, because resisting is not among the things she has ever been able to usefully do.

choices.label: Let the arrangement stand
choices.outcomeText: You paid the rate and it is remembered as a rate paid. The next party to need her pays slightly more, and she sees none of the difference.

choices.label: Offer to carry her escort yourself
choices.outcomeText: It is the first offer of its kind she has had. It also means she travels under your colors, which she understands perfectly well and accepts anyway, having compared it honestly against the alternative.

choices.label: Hold her
choices.outcomeText: She works, competently and without complaint, and is worth every bit of what she is supposed to be worth. A wire-reader who has been taken once is worth less to everybody afterward, including to whoever took her, and the reason is not sentiment: nobody will now send her anywhere she might be taken from.

choices.label: Protect the grade
choices.outcomeText: You stop the quarrying, which makes you unpopular with four settlements and gives you two miles of the best road in the district. Nobody can build another one and everybody can build another wall.

choices.label: Quarry it properly
choices.outcomeText: If it is going to be taken apart it may as well be taken apart by people who can cut and stack. You get a great deal of the finest dressed stone anybody here will ever handle, out of the last flat two miles in the district.

choices.label: Leave them to it
choices.outcomeText: It goes on at the pace it has gone on at for thirty years, which means the grade has perhaps another thirty in it, which means it is somebody else's decision.

choices.label: Keep the road open
choices.outcomeText: Freight moves across this district faster than it moves anywhere within a hundred miles, and the four settlements that hate you for it use it constantly.

choices.label: Put the stone to use
choices.outcomeText: It builds well. It builds better than anything anybody could quarry fresh. There is a granary footing under your settlement now that will outlast the settlement, laid in material off the last flat road in the country.

choices.label: Say nothing about it
choices.outcomeText: Two more sections come out over the winter, into a byre wall. The wagons go round.

choices.label: Fund the standard
choices.outcomeText: The jig is built, the three joiners are found other work or are not, and by autumn a window frame costs a third of what it cost in spring. The settlement begins, subtly and permanently, to look like something that was planned.

choices.label: Keep the joiners
choices.outcomeText: Three men keep their trade and their methods and their pride, and every building you put up for the rest of your life costs what it costs.

choices.label: Let them compete
choices.outcomeText: They compete. The builder underbids the joiners on everything and the joiners do the work the jig cannot, badly and late, out of spite. You get the standard eventually and you get it with four men who will not speak to each other.

choices.label: Send him east
choices.outcomeText: He is gone a long time — longer than he said, longer than you budgeted for — and what comes back is a man who can do one thing nobody else here can do and who is now, unmistakably, somebody who has been to the foundries.

choices.label: Go on buying them
choices.outcomeText: They are cheap, they are better than anything you make, and there is no moment at which the decision to keep buying them is the wrong one.

choices.label: Have him try it here
choices.outcomeText: He fails. He fails four times, expensively, and on the fifth he produces something that is not a casting and is not the bolted part either, and works better than both for reasons he can explain at length to anyone who will stand still.

choices.label: Let it stand
choices.outcomeText: The small things go to her and the large things come to you, and the line between them is drawn by everybody except you, continuously, without anyone discussing it.

choices.label: Forbid her taking disputes
choices.outcomeText: She complies at once, entirely without argument, and goes on receiving people in her front room who arrive with disputes and leave having discussed the weather. Everyone understands the arrangement. It is now yours to keep pretending not to.

choices.label: Put her on retainer
choices.outcomeText: She takes it, names a fee that is high and fair, and from that week the judgments handed down in her front room are handed down in your name. She is better at it than you are. You have bought that, and everyone knows what it cost.

choices.label: Let it go up
choices.outcomeText: It goes up. It will be there longer than you will.
